target_customer: Online shoppers who miss home deliveries, and small senders who want a drop-off point for UPS, USPS or FedEx shipments
problem: Missed deliveries and stolen packages at home, and the hassle of packaging and posting items to ship.
business_model: Consumer fee per package received (free first package, then 1.99 USD each) plus shipping margin on outbound parcels, with kiosks hosted in local businesses

founders.name: Neel Murthy
education: Left Stanford MS in CS (AI) and a deferred Stanford GSB MBA to join YC
founders.background_notes: Later Chief Growth at Goldbelly and Head of Growth at Rippling per his YC profile.

founders.name: Nitin Shantharam
founders.background_notes: No biography on the YC page.

competitors.name: BufferBox
competitors.what: Canadian parcel locker network that Google then acquired and moved toward the Bay Area
competitors.traction_then: Lockers in Canada, first US station in San Francisco in April 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware kiosks built from modified gym lockers with touchscreen, notifications and carrier integrations for UPS, USPS and FedEx, plus site installation logistics, were hard for a two person team but used off the shelf parts.

defensibility.rationale: Locker host locations and multi merchant support were its edge, but hardware was copyable and Amazon and Google had deeper pockets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google bought BufferBox in 2012 and Amazon expanded Lockers from 2013; Swapbox is listed inactive, with the cause not public.

market_need_then: Missed delivery notices and package theft were common complaints as online shopping grew, and coverage in 2013 framed the BufferBox acquisition as leaving a gap for a multi retailer locker service.

branding.domain_note: Used swapbox.com; the site no longer resolves from the research environment.

identity.visual_style: Custom industrial design on kiosk hardware; the CEO said they focused on industrial design to help branding

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage by TechCrunch, ABC7 and Bloomberg; no evidence of community, merch or memes.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered in tech press but no sign of a distinctive brand asset, and the name is easily confused with the Danish locker maker SwipBox.

outcome_analysis: Swapbox launched from YC W13 into the gap left by Google's BufferBox purchase, raised 800K in December 2013 and had about 22 kiosks in San Francisco by 2014 with an A round planned. It is now listed as inactive, and the cause of the shutdown is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Outcome searches found no shutdown post-mortem or acquisition news; the cause is not public. Seedtable lists a 2.2M seed in May 2015 with Trevor Blackwell, single aggregator source, unverified and not recorded as a round. CB Insights lists a 2021 seed with no amount, likely a different entity. swapbox.com did not resolve in the research environment. Do not confuse with SwipBox of Denmark.
